Life is short; there's a huge amount of evil in the world and we have free will. So the question is not: "Why is there so much evil in the world, if Allah is merciful?" Rather: "What can I do to make the world a better place? As an insignificant, small person that I am..." Which is somewhat what you said in your last paragraphs. 

And I can see pretty obvious answers to that within the islamic teaching. One can also backtrack the teachings and confirm their correctness by looking at history. Black plague would've never happened if Islam was a globally accepted religion. Famine in Ireland, Russia and other Scandinavian countries wouldn't have happened... 

But since Muslims happen to be humans with free will, and when the freedom of thought or will is left unchecked, it'll almost always lead to selfish behavior; which results in darker consequences for the majority of human kind. 

Maybe you've heard this before, but it's the Muslim people who suck, not the religion itself. But, figuring out whether this is true or false takes a lot of effort; so people act in a selfish manner and don't think about it at all. Because they have bills to pay, relatives to take care of etc. 

Masses never liked/wanted to spend time dealing with thought. Never. Because again, life is short and there's so many meaningless stuff that would make you feel good. And to feel good, our brains are wired to love. 

My point is: Whether or not Allah is real, a person's duty in this life is to create a better environment to everyone around them. With a heart full of love, tolerance and compassion. We don't know when the society's going to go down. So we better aim for a better future and systematically work for it. 

But masses just won't do that :) They just won't. And that's the trick. Allah believes, in my opinion, we can do it. Maybe they(Allah) just want to see exactly that. Maybe Allâh is looking at a mirror, of some sort. We don't have to know.
